questions: Does the 10 mm pitch give a usable graded signal, or does it saturate (all sensors fully on or off the tape) on the bends?
Is the 0.04 m forward offset helpful for lookahead, or does it cause lag and oscillation on the sharper bends?
Is the 12 mm footprint the right size for the 25 mm tape, or would 8 mm or 16 mm give better resolution or more robust line loss behaviour?
Does the 0.8 kg mass and 0.12 m track limit the achievable speed, and does the robot reach the progress needed in under 3 s?

intent: Baseline geometry: five sensors at 10 mm pitch spanning 40 mm across the line, 12 mm footprints matched to the 25 mm tape, sensors 0.04 m ahead of the axle for lookahead, and a mid-range chassis (0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.8 kg). This establishes a reference point so later iterations can change one geometric variable at a time, guided by the Integrator's feedback on how the sensors behave in practice.
learning: No prior races, so nothing has been learned yet. Next iteration, compare the baseline's rms_error and line_loss_events against the sensor-pitch and forward-offset hypotheses, and change only one geometric variable at a time.
rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry and no Integrator feedback, so this proposal is a neutral baseline meant to make the first race informative. The 25 mm tape is covered by a 12 mm sensor footprint, so a 5-sensor bar at 10 mm pitch (x = -0.02 to +0.02) always has at least two sensors reading tape on a centred line. That gives a graded signal and avoids the line-loss threshold on small deviations. The sensors sit 0.04 m ahead of the axle so the reading leads the wheels by a few centimetres, which gives the controller some lookahead for the bends. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a mid-range turn authority and a top speed that can plausibly reach the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s. Mass 0.8 kg keeps inertia moderate. Body width 0.12 m keeps the off-track limit at 0.06 m, the floor of max(0.06, tape_half_width + body_width/4), so the robot is not given extra slack. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with the slalom as the harder test. I expect the line-loss and rms_error metrics to show whether the 10 mm pitch is too fine or too coarse, and whether the sensors are too far ahead for the bends.
